title: Retrospective common-support comparison of a custom adversarial residual-ranking MLP and standard baselines

design.target: Next-calendar-month simple return, never imputed; fitted target is the standardized within-training-month average rank, with degenerate training periods mapped to zero.
design.features: Five complete-calendar lagged-return/volatility controls and seven recomputed disclosure-count, buy-share and announcement-delay features; all fitted models use the same 12 features.
design.split: Expanding annual training with observed labels that mature no later than the fit cutoff; model weights fixed within each evaluation year.
design.preprocessing: Finite training-only feature medians, with all-missing training features filled by zero, followed by training-only means and population standard deviations.
design.custom_neural_model: Actual raw-rank and two-way-residual-rank losses, gradient-reversal issuer/month heads and stability penalty; two 128-unit layers, 20 fixed epochs, three fixed seeds. Each seed score is 0.25 times its raw head plus its residual head.
design.ensemble: Arithmetic mean of all three fixed seed scores; individual seeds are reported without selection.
design.ridge: Ridge regression with alpha 10, fitted to the same training rank target.
design.histogram_gradient_boosting: 200 iterations, learning rate 0.05, 15 leaves, minimum leaf size 30, L2 regularization 1, no early stopping.
design.unfit_control: One-month momentum from a complete preceding calendar month; missing values use the same training median.
design.selection: No hyperparameter selection, epoch selection, outcome-dependent stopping, security sampling or transaction replication.

metrics.primary: Equal-weight mean within-month Spearman over common eligible periods with at least ten rows and nonconstant outcomes and every reported score.
secondary: Standard deviation of within-month Spearman values on the same eligible periods

limitations: The source extracts do not provide historical snapshots or publication/ingestion timestamps for transaction revisions, revised-primary security mappings, price adjustments, or dividends. Historical vintages are unverified.

Transaction uniqueness is checked against the current full extract, and security identifiers and adjusted prices are current-source fields. The cohort is therefore selected retrospectively; verified train-only preprocessing and label-maturity checks do not establish historical availability of the evaluation population.
Reported announcement days are filtered against forecast origins but have not been independently matched against archived original public announcements.

The population is a conservative subset of covered securities with eligible disclosures and observed next-calendar-month outcomes. Vendor coverage, missing outcomes and delisting selection remain limitations; missing labels are not imputed.
The comparison uses 12 conservative available features and is neither a reconstruction nor a reranking of the historical 30-model comparison.
Ridge and histogram gradient boosting use fixed settings. This is not an exhaustive hyperparameter competition or an ablation of every component of the custom neural objective.
The evaluation concerns temporal prediction within the covered security population; it does not establish generalization to held-out securities.
Annual model weights are fixed after the fit cutoff. The assumption that the relevant data are observable after the calendar day ends is not verified by historical market-data publication records.

The comparison was recorded before its own fits, but these reconstructed outcomes had already been used for a different simple-MLP experiment. It is not an untouched prospective holdout or an external preregistration.
Metrics are descriptive. No confidence intervals, significance tests, finite certificate, prospective validity, economic-profitability claim or model selection is supported by this export.
No external archive retrieval, pretrained checkpoints or reconstruction of all historical models was used.
